`let expected = 9_223_372_036_854_775_802;` is 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFA, which Clippy 0.1.99 reports (clippy_lints/src/literal_representation.rs, DecimalLiteralRepresentation::check_lit and do_lint: `val >= threshold`, then a hexadecimal representation of 4 digits or more whose first digit is 7 and whose middle digits are all F). The rule language has no hexadecimal reading of a value, so the port reads the digits as `value` ranges and `bitsAny` masks, and a bundled rule's text reaches the engine through JavaScript (src/engine/code-rule/code-rule-dsl-catalog.ts compiles stableJsonText of the parsed document), whose numbers are IEEE-754 doubles: 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFF0 (9223372036854775792) and 2^63 both become 9223372036854776000, so the range this literal needs is empty, and no power of two from 2^55 to 2^69 (the masks and bounds of every digit there) keeps its value. The port reads values below 2^53 only (its description says so). The engine reads the literal's value exactly; the rule cannot name it.

This port is the variant for `literal-representation-threshold = 0xFFFFFF` (tests/ui-toml/decimal_literal_representation/clippy.toml), under which the literal is below the threshold; the corpus was recorded with Clippy's default threshold, 16384, under which the default port reports the same line (TP).
